V.}}}}}}

{{c|''Curing a bedred man at the pond of miracle, becau{{ls}}e he doth it on the Sabboth, the blind Ievves do per{{ls}}ecute him, 7 and againe becau{{ls}}e he {{ls}}aith that God is his natural father. 19 He therevpon continueth {{ls}}aying, the Fathers operation and his to be in euery thing al one, and that he {{ls}}hal do greater things then the{{ls}}e miraculous cures, to vvit, 21 quicken the dead in {{ls}}oule by {{ls}}inne, as being appointed Iudge of al, 28 yea and quicken the dead in bodies al{{ls}}o. incontinent iudging al vprightly. 31 And that the{{ls}}e are not bragges of his owne, but his vvitne{{ls}}{{ls}}es to be, 33 Iohn Bapti{{ls}}t, 36 his owne miraculous vvorkes, 37 his fathers voice at his bapti{{ls}}me, 39 the Scriptures al{{ls}}o, namely of Moy{{ls}}es.''}}

{{dropinitial|A|fl={{verse|chapter=5|verse=1}}}}{{sc|Fter}} {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Go{{ls}}pel vpō friday in the fir{{ls}}t weeke of Lent.}}the{{ls}}e things there vvas a fe{{ls}}tiual day of the Ievves, and {{sc|Iesvs}} vvent vp to Hieru{{ls}}alem. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=2}} And there is at Hieru{{ls}}alem `vpon' {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ By our latin text and the Greeke, this miraculous pond was in or vpon ''Probatica'', that is, a place vvhere the {{ls}}heepe to be {{ls}}acrificed, vvere kept. But by other latin copies, S. Hierom, and {{ls}}ome Greeke fathers, ''Probatica'' is the very pōd it {{ls}}elf: {{ls}}o called, becau{{ls}}e the {{ls}}heepe of {{ls}}acrifice vvere there wa{{ls}}hed.}}∷ Probatica {{sup|‖}} a pond vvhich in hebrevv is {{ls}}urnamed {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''`Bethe{{ls}}da,''}}`Beth{{ls}}aida', hauing fiue porches. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=3}} In the{{ls}}e lay a great multitude of {{ls}}icke per{{ls}}ons, of blinde, lame, vvithered, expecting the {{ls}}tirring of the vvater. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=4}} And an Angel of our Lord de{{ls}}cended at a certaine time into the pond: and the vvater vvas {{ls}}tirred. And he that had gone dovvne fir{{ls}}t into the pond after the {{ls}}tirring of the vvater, vvas made vvhole of vvhat{{ls}}oeuer infirmitie he vvas holden. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=5}} And there vvas a certaine man there that had been eight and thirtie yeres in his infirmitie. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=6}} Him when {{sc|Iesvs}} had {{ls}}een lying, & knevv that c {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''multū tempus haberet'',}}∷ he had novv a long time, he {{ls}}aith to him, Vvilt thou be made vvhole? {{verse|chapter=5|verse=7}} The {{ls}}icke man an{{ls}}vvered him, Lord, I haue no man, vvhen the vvater is troubled, to put me into the pond. For vvhiles I come, an other goeth dovvne before me. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=8}} {{sc|Iesvs}} {{ls}}aith to him, Ari{{ls}}e, take vp thy bed, and vvalke. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=9}} And forthvvith he vvas made vvhole: and he tooke vp his bed, and vvalked. And it vvas the Sabboth that day. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=10}} The Ievves therfore {{ls}}aid to him that vvas healed, It is the Sabboth, thou mai{{ls}}t not take vp thy bed. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=11}} He an{{ls}}wered them, He that made me vvhole, he {{ls}}aid to me, Take vp thy bed, and walke. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=12}} They a{{ls}}ked him therfore, VVhat is that man that {{ls}}aid to thee, Take vp thy bed, and vvalke? {{verse|chapter=5|verse=13}} But he that vvas made vvhole, knevv not vvho it vvas. For {{sc|Iesvs}} {{ls}}hronke a{{ls}}ide from the multitude {{ls}}tanding in the place. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=14}} Aftervvard {{sc|Iesvs}} findeth him in the temple, and {{ls}}aid to him, Behold thou art made vvhole: {{sup|‖}} {{ls}}inne no more, le{{ls}}t {{ls}}ome vvor{{ls}}e thing chaunce to thee. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=15}} That man vvent his vvay, and told the Ievves that it was {{sc|Iesvs}} that made him whole.⊣ {{verse|chapter=5|verse=16}} Therevpon the Iewes per{{ls}}ecuted {{sc|Iesvs}}, becau{{ls}}e he did the{{ls}}e things on the Sabboth.

{{verse|chapter=5|verse=17}} But {{sc|Iesvs}} an{{ls}}vvered them, My father vvorketh vntil novv: and I doe vvorke. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=18}} Therevpō therefore the Ievves {{ls}}ought the more to kil him: becau{{ls}}e he did not only breake the Sabboth, but al{{ls}}o he {{ls}}aid God was his father, making him {{ls}}elf aequal to God. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=19}} {{sc|Iesvs}} therfore an{{ls}}vvered, and {{ls}}aid to them, Amen, amen I {{ls}}ay to you, The Sonne can not doe any thing of him {{ls}}elf, but that vvhich he {{ls}}eeth the Father doing.<noinclude>{{continues|For}}</noinclude>
